poems:
Court is in session.
The witness is you, nineteen, in a Denny's parking lot.

2:01. The refrigerator kicks on, does its work, kicks off,
and gets nothing for it.
Break room, folding chair, still warm.

Somewhere over the Atlantic a cart comes up the aisle
with water nobody asked for.

Do not check the phone.
Do not open the fridge.
Open the fridge.

The dog relocates to the cool tile,
official about it.

2:06, and the humidifier has been out of water for hours,
running anyway.
A night nurse three rooms down, laughing at something on her phone.
Insomnia, n. a meeting you called and cannot adjourn.
Ice maker, full drop, like a body.

Ten past two.
The neighbor's motion light finds a cat, then nothing, then a cat.
Somewhere this is lunch.

One Gatorade, one lighter, one banana.
Sold at 2:12 a.m.

The house makes the noise it has made every night for eleven years,
and tonight it is a man.
In the walk-in, dough rises without supervision.

Quarter past two, and the mind produces a name
you have not needed since 1994,
and offers it up like a gift.
Toll plaza, one car, no line.
Through the wall: no, no, I'm up, I'm up.

A new father in a recliner with a bottle,
and a documentary about volcanoes
he will not remember in the morning.

2:19. The scrolling has gone past today's posts
and into archaeology.
Moth against the porch bulb, still at it.

Two twenty-one at the plant. Lunch, per the contract.
Somebody heats a plate and calls it noon.

The last bus of the night is the first bus of the morning
and it is empty either way.
Somebody's mother is up too, three states over, doing exactly this.
Water on the nightstand, gone flat.

Tomorrow: the tire, the dentist,
the email from March,
the tire.
2:26, and the cat has business elsewhere in the house.
Hospital vending machine, C4, stuck.

You could get up. People get up.
There is an entire population of people who got up.
Freight train, two miles off, taking its time.
Half past two. The exact middle of nobody's day.
Truck stop, shower seven called twice, no takers.

The furnace. The pipes. The settling.
The neighbor's dryer.
The blood in the ear.

Drafted, deleted, drafted again, not sent.
2:33.
The ER doors open for no one, close, open again.

Everyone who loves you is asleep.
That is a scheduling problem, not a verdict.

A pallet jack in aisle nine at the 24-hour Kroger,
and the man pushing it is singing.

2:37. Reheated in a break room: rice,
and something that used to be chicken.
The bar's floor mats are out on the sidewalk, hosed and steaming.

A password from a job that ended in 2011,
recalled perfectly, unrequested.

The mind offers the tire, the biopsy,
and the thing said at the funeral.
It does not rank them.

2:41 a.m. is a fine time to remember
that you never wrote back to Denise.
Radio tower, red, red, red.

Two forty-three. The bakers' alarms are twenty minutes out.
Theirs will go off. Theirs will work.

Name five things in the room.
Then five more.
This works about a third of the time.
Two forty-five, and the thermostat clicks like it has an opinion.
Boot dryer running in the mudroom, for nobody.
The tow truck driver eats a sandwich in the cab with the engine running.

2:48. Somebody is being told something in a hallway
and will remember the tile for the rest of her life.
The dryer downstairs finishes its cycle and buzzes for whoever.

Reason for visit:
and then the handwriting getting worse
toward the bottom of the page.

The mind, done with 1994, moves on to
what you might say at your own retirement party.
Mile marker 118, cruise set at 63.

2:53. The phone at four percent,
and no decision made about that.

An office tower with one floor lit,
cleaning crew on eleven.

Five to three, and the good idea arrives.
It will not survive the shower.
An owl, or a dove, or a man doing one badly.

2:57. Nothing has been decided.
Everything has been reviewed.

Two minutes is plenty of time to fall asleep.
It has never once been enough.

One minute left in the audit.
The auditor requests an extension.
